Chicken with Almonds & Eggs

Moroccan · Medium · Serves 4–6

Jump to Recipe Method Troubleshooting Storage
Djej b'stèn — chicken with almonds and eggs — is the pastilla's (#38's) weekday sister and the celebration table's own argument: chicken slow-cooked in the saffron-onion base until the sauce runs silk, then bound at the end with beaten eggs that set to soft curds through the sauce, and crowned with fried almonds and a whisper of cinnamon. The egg-thickened tagine is the canon's distinctive register — a sauce that binds to a sliceable, spoonable richness — and this record is its master.

Quantities live in the recipe card.

Ingredients

  • the #38's own almond doctrine, carried
  • the whisper-crown, dusted in a single fine line
- **Cook the chicken to the sauce's concentration before the eggs join.** The egg-thickened tagine's law: the onions must dissolve entirely and the broth reduce to a scant, intense silk — the eggs set in that concentrated sauce, and a watery base makes curds in a soup, not the bound richness the dish is. The bridge: none needed; the whole row is the daily shelf. - **The almonds' clock:** fried to deep gold and crushed coarse — the #38 pastilla's own almond doctrine, carried at the weekday scale. The cinnamon-sugar's whisper: a pinch, not a dusting — this is a savory dish with a sweet's crown.

Doneness & Quality Checkpoints

  • The base: onions dissolved, the sauce a concentrated centimeter before the eggs.
  • The binding: the pot cooled, the eggs stirred one direction, the curds set soft.
  • The crown: fried almonds crushed coarse, the cinnamon-sugar whispered.

Chicken with Almonds & Eggs

Prep: 30 minutes, plus 1 hour marinating · Cook: 1 hour 10 minutes · Total: About 2 hours 45 minutes · Serves 4–6

Ingredients

Ingredients

  • 1 chicken (about 1.4 kg), cut to 8 pieces
  • 3 onions (about 450 g), grated; 5 cloves garlic (about 20 g), grated
  • 1 tsp saffron (about 1 g) in 3 tbsp warm water (#120); 1½ tsp ginger; ½ tsp turmeric; ½ tsp cinnamon; ½ tsp white pepper
  • 2 tbsp butter (about 30 g); 1½ tsp salt; a fist of cilantro and parsley (about 25 g), tied
  • 400 ml water (about 400 g)
  • 4 eggs (about 200 g), beaten
  • 100 g almonds (about 100 g), fried to deep gold in 2 tbsp neutral oil (about 25 g) and coarsely crushed — the #38's own almond doctrine, carried
  • 1 tsp cinnamon (about 2 g) mixed with 1 tbsp powdered sugar (about 8 g) — the whisper-crown, dusted in a single fine line
  • The juice of ½ a lemon (about 15 ml); bread or the #34 couscous to serve

Instructions

  1. **The long base (1 hour at the tremble).** Melt the butter in the tagine or heavy pot; the chicken turned in the aromatics, saffron water, and spices 4 minutes to the perfume; the water and the herbs — cover, tremble (95 °C), and cook 1 hour, until the chicken is tender and the onions have melted to a golden, saffron-scented silk barely a centimeter deep. Checkpoint — the base's end: a scant, intense gold — the spoon's coat heavy — and the chicken at the bone's yield. If the sauce runs deeper than a centimeter, uncover 10 minutes and reduce: the eggs' binding demands the concentration.
  2. **The eggs' binding (4 minutes, the dish's own craft).** Off the flame, let the pot cool 2 minutes (the eggs' mercy — a boiling pot scrambles them to rubber); pour in the beaten eggs slowly, stirring constantly in one direction, and return to the lowest flame 2–3 minutes more, stirring, until the sauce sets to soft curds through the silk — a bound, spoonable mass that mounds and holds. Checkpoint — the bound sauce's test: a spoonful holds its shape on the plate's edge — the eggs' curds running through the onion's silk, the whole a sliceable-rich register that no cream and no reduction achieves. The taste: savory-deep, the saffron forward, the cinnamon's whisper beneath.
  3. **The crown and the table.** Off the heat: the lemon's juice through, the crushed almonds scattered over in their gold, the cinnamon-sugar's whisper dusted in a fine line — and the pot to the table with the bread. Checkpoint — eating test, with bread: the chicken's saffron silk and the egg-bound sauce's richness — each scoop holding sauce and meat together, the almonds' toast and crunch between, the cinnamon-sugar's faint sweetness arriving at the swallow over the savory depth. It should taste like the pastilla's argument made weeknight: the same elements (chicken, almonds, the cinnamon's whisper), the bread standing in for the warqa, and the eggs binding the whole to the canon's most distinctive sauce.

Finish & Plate

The tagine to the table — the egg-bound gold under the almonds' scatter, the cinnamon's line — bread at every hand, and the pot's spoon serving sauce and meat in each scoop, which is the bound sauce's own service.

Troubleshooting

SymptomCauseFix
Eggs scrambled to rubberPot too hot at the pourThe two-minute cool; the lowest flame's return
Sauce refused to bindBase watery or eggs under-stirredThe centimeter's concentration; one direction, constant
Dish heavy past pleasureThe lemon skippedThe finish's cut is structural

Storage, Make-Ahead & Variations

- The base keeps 3 days (the eggs always bound at the reheat's service, the doctrine's freshness); the bound pot keeps 1 day and re-warms gently, covered. The #38 pastilla is this record's grand expression. - Variations: the kefta's egg-bound cousin (#33's register), the lamb version. The #120 saffron and the #34 couscous are this pot's parents.
